chapter_en: Chapter of Judgments by Example for the Eight Palaces

units.chapter: 旁通部·十、四时吉凶神杀例
units.chapter_en: Parallel Tables, Section 10: Auspicious and Ominous Spirit-Stars of the Four Seasons
units.title: 四时吉凶神杀例·占病要忌的三个煞：五墓(春未夏戌秋丑冬辰)发动持凶；浴盆(春辰夏未秋戌冬丑)临水神水爻并凶；三丘(春丑夏辰秋未冬戌)发动兄鬼主死

rule.yi: 周易尚占旁通部的「四时吉凶神杀例」表列了三个占病要忌的煞，位置按春、夏、秋、冬的次序排：五墓是未、戌、丑、辰，发动、持（世）都凶；浴盆是辰、未、戌、丑，落在水神（玄武）或水爻上都凶；三丘是丑、辰、未、戌，发动、又有兄弟或官鬼，主死。
rule.en: The table of auspicious and ominous spirit-stars of the four seasons in the Parallel Tables of the Zhouyi Shangzhan lists three stars to avoid in asking about illness, set out in the order spring, summer, autumn, winter: the Five Tombs at Wei, Xu, Chou, Chen, ominous when they move or hold the Self; the Bathing Basin at Chen, Wei, Xu, Chou, ominous when it falls on a Water spirit (the Dark Tortoise) or a Water line; the Three Mounds at Chou, Chen, Wei, Xu, which mean death when they move together with Peer or Pressure.

zh: 五墓未戌丑辰占病忌之，
浴盆辰未戌丑占病忌之，
三丘丑辰未戌占病忌之，
yi: 五墓：未、戌、丑、辰（依春、夏、秋、冬的次序），占病要忌它，
浴盆：辰、未、戌、丑，占病要忌它，
三丘：丑、辰、未、戌，占病要忌它，
en: The four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, winter.
Five Tombs: Wei, Xu, Chou, Chen (in the order spring, summer, autumn, winter); in asking about illness avoid it,
if it moves or holds [the Self], it is ominous.
Bathing Basin: Chen, Wei, Xu, Chou; in asking about illness avoid it,
falling on a Water spirit or a Water line, both are ominous.
Three Mounds: Chou, Chen, Wei, Xu; in asking about illness avoid it,
if it moves, with Peer or Pressure, it means death.

note.yi: 这三行是周易尚占旁通部「十、四时吉凶神杀例」表的末三行，表头是春夏秋冬，每个煞的四个地支按这个次序排。三丘、五墓的位置和断易天机（LY.ILL.DYTJ.31）、易林补遗（LY.ILL.EL.51）一致：三丘春丑夏辰秋未冬戌，五墓取三丘的对宫（春未夏戌秋丑冬辰）。浴盆的位置（春辰夏未秋戌冬丑）和卜筮全书神煞歌例里的沐浴杀（LY.ILL.BSQS.53）、疾病论里的催尸杀（LY.ILL.BSQS.36）一样，书里没有说它们是不是同一个煞；卜筮全书「四般休问病」里的浴盆只点了名、没有给位置（LY.ILL.BSQS.11）。「发动持凶」的「持」书里没有写「世」，译文照一般的用法读作持世，放在方括号里；「临水神水爻并凶」「发动兄鬼主死」书里都没有写主语，译文补成「它」。「水神」按这一部前面「十一、定六神」里的「青龙木神，朱雀火神，勾陈土神，白虎金神，玄武水神」（第 461 行），是玄武；「兄鬼」是兄弟、官鬼。同一部分前面的合刑杀例（六合、三合、三刑、驿马、劫杀、亡神、咸池）不管病，这里不收。
note.en: These are the last three rows of the table 'Section 10: Auspicious and Ominous Spirit-Stars of the Four Seasons' in the Parallel Tables of the Zhouyi Shangzhan; the header row is spring, summer, autumn, winter, and the four branches of each star follow that order. The positions of the Three Mounds and the Five Tombs agree with the Duanyi Tianji (LY.ILL.DYTJ.31) and the Yilin Buyi (LY.ILL.EL.51): the Three Mounds are Chou in spring, Chen in summer, Wei in autumn, Xu in winter, and the Five Tombs are taken from the opposite palace of the Three Mounds (Wei in spring, Xu in summer, Chou in autumn, Chen in winter). The positions of the Bathing Basin (Chen in spring, Wei in summer, Xu in autumn, Chou in winter) are the same as those of the Bathing killing in the verses of spirit-stars of the Bushi Quanshu (LY.ILL.BSQS.53) and of the Corpse-Urging killing in its essay on illness (LY.ILL.BSQS.36); the books do not say whether they are the same star, and the Bathing Basin in the Bushi Quanshu's 'four kinds not to ask about illness' is only named, with no positions given (LY.ILL.BSQS.11). The 'hold' of 'if it moves or holds, it is ominous' is not followed by 'the Self' in the book; the translation reads it in the usual way as holding the Self, and puts that in square brackets; neither 'falling on a Water spirit or a Water line, both ominous' nor 'if it moves, with Peer or Pressure, it means death' has a subject in the book, and the translation supplies 'it'. 'Water spirit' is, by the earlier section 'Section 11: Fixing the Six Spirits' in the same part, with its 'Azure Dragon is the Wood spirit, Vermilion Bird the Fire spirit, Hook Earth the Earth spirit, White Tiger the Metal spirit, Dark Tortoise the Water spirit' (line 461), the Dark Tortoise; 'Peer or Pressure' stands for the two characters meaning 'brother' and 'ghost'. The table of combining, punishing and killing stars before it in the same part (six combinations, three harmonies, three punishments, post horse, robbery, loss, bathing pool) is not about illness and is not taken here.

units.chapter_en: Chapter of Judgments by Example for the Eight Palaces
units.title: 八卦断例·占病逢观、大有、大畜、损、无妄、兑、谦：病痊、病瘥、病脱(病会好)

rule.yi: 周易尚占的八卦断例是一卦一行断辞，下面七个卦的断辞明说病会好：观「财聚病痊」，大有「讼散病痊」，大畜「婚成病脱」，损「婚成病瘥」，无妄「病瘥讼和」，兑「病瘥婚成」，谦「身吉病瘥」。痊、瘥是痊愈，病脱是病脱去了。
rule.en: In the judgments by example of the Zhouyi Shangzhan each hexagram has one line of verdicts, and in these seven the line says outright that the illness will be well: Guan, 'wealth gathers, the illness is cured'; Dayou, 'the lawsuit disperses, the illness is cured'; Daxu, 'marriage is made, the illness drops away'; Sun, 'marriage is made, the illness is cured'; Wuwang, 'the illness is cured, the lawsuit is settled'; Dui, 'the illness is cured, marriage is made'; Qian (Humility), 'the person is fortunate, the illness is cured'. 'Cured' and 'recovered' both mean full recovery, and 'drops away' means the illness is shed.

en: Wealth gathers and the illness is cured.
What is sought will surely come.
Fields and house prosper and flourish.
The lawsuit disperses and the illness is cured.
Pregnancy comes to birth and marriage is achieved.
Fields ripen and silkworms are harvested.
Marriage is made and the illness drops away.
The person and dwelling are middling.
Marriage is made and the illness is cured.
The household is favourable and upright.
In all matters follow what is real.
Keeping to the old is supremely auspicious.
The illness is cured and the lawsuit settled.
Fields give harvest and wealth accumulates.
Illness is cured and marriage is made.
Pregnancy comes to birth and calamity retreats.
The person and dwelling are safe.
The six domestic animals bring wealth.
Soft and modest, knowing when to stop.
Do not ask about moving house.
As for a lawsuit, let it rest.
The person is fortunate and the illness is cured.

dispute.yi: 按卦名断病，各书不一样，而这七个卦里的观、大畜，别的书说占病凶。观卦：这里说「财聚病痊」，可是阐奥歌章（LY.ILL.CA.03）说「夏观」凶，卜筮全书疾病论（LY.ILL.BSQS.35）说「夏嫌观蛊」，卜筮元龟一段（LY.ILL.DYTJ.15）和阐奥歌章第五首（LY.ILL.CA.06）都把观列进占病的凶卦，天玄赋（LY.ILL.TXF.06）说观「切忌世身入墓」（有条件的），增删卜易（LY.ILL.ZS.01）转述的「断之必死」的十个卦里也有观、大畜。大畜卦这里说「婚成病脱」，天玄赋却说大畜「莫逢财鬼俱兴」。另一方面，野鹤（LY.ILL.ZS.01）和易林补遗（LY.ILL.EL.13）根本反对按卦名断病，说断病全凭用神、「休把卦名推祸福」。书里没有裁决。
dispute.en: Judging illness by hexagram name differs from book to book, and of these seven the other books call Guan and Daxu ominous for illness. Guan: here it says 'wealth gathers, the illness is cured', but the Chan'ao Gezhang (LY.ILL.CA.03) calls 'Guan in summer' ominous, the Bushi Quanshu's essay on illness (LY.ILL.BSQS.35) says 'summer dislikes Guan and Gu', the passage of the Bushi Yuangui (LY.ILL.DYTJ.15) and the fifth poem of the Chan'ao Gezhang (LY.ILL.CA.06) both put Guan among the ominous hexagrams for illness, the Tianxuan Fu (LY.ILL.TXF.06) says of Guan 'above all avoid the Self or the Body entering the tomb' (a conditional statement), and the ten hexagrams of 'judge death' reported in the Zengshan Buyi (LY.ILL.ZS.01) include Guan and Daxu. For Daxu the line here says 'marriage is made, the illness drops away', while the Tianxuan Fu says of Daxu 'do not meet Wealth and Pressure both stirring'. On the other side, the Old Man of Yehe (LY.ILL.ZS.01) and the Yilin Buyi (LY.ILL.EL.13) are against judging illness by hexagram name at all, saying that life and death in illness rest wholly on the Subject, 'do not push fortune and misfortune from the name of the hexagram'. The books do not decide.

note.yi: 八卦断例章一卦一行断辞，每行八个词组：头一个解释卦名的字义，后面几个分别讲事、人口、田蚕、官司、婚姻、出行、病、孕等。所以病只是其中的一个词组，这里把整行录出来，病的那一句在观卦是第七个、大有第五个、大畜第六个、损第三个、无妄第五个、兑第三个、谦第七个词组。这些断辞只按卦名给，没有讲用神、世应、动变，也不分近病久病。大有卦这一行开头没有「X者Y也」的释名，是「盛大丰育」四个字，照原文。第三个卦「畜者聚也」是大畜（艮宫第三卦），不是小畜，小畜另有一行「小畜止也」，那一行没有讲病，这里不用。「病脱」的「脱」是病去掉了。原文里整行没有标点，词组之间只有空格，译文分词组对齐。
note.en: The chapter of judgments by example gives each hexagram one line of verdicts, in eight phrases: the first explains the sense of the hexagram's name, and the rest speak in turn of affairs, household members, fields and silkworms, lawsuits, marriage, travel, illness, pregnancy and so on. Illness is therefore only one phrase among them, and the whole line is taken here, with the phrase on illness being the seventh for Guan, the fifth for Dayou, the sixth for Daxu, the third for Sun, the fifth for Wuwang, the third for Dui and the seventh for Qian (Humility). These verdicts are given by hexagram name alone, with nothing said of the Subject, Self and Other or moving lines, and no distinction between recent and long illness. The line of Dayou has no explanation of the name of the form 'X means Y' at its head, but the four characters 'flourishing, grand, abundant, nourishing', as in the original. The 'Xu means gathering' of the third hexagram is Daxu (the third hexagram of the Gen palace) and not Xiaoxu, which has a line of its own, 'Xiaoxu means holding back', that does not speak of illness and is not used here. The 'drops away' of 'the illness drops away' is the illness being shed. The whole line has no punctuation in the original, only spaces between the phrases, and the translation is aligned phrase by phrase.

units.chapter_en: Chapter of Judgments by Example for the Eight Palaces
units.title: 八卦断例·占病逢乾、既济、革、贲、渐、豫、解、随、家人、益、颐、鼎、比、萃、咸：病安、安康、安宁、无忧、俱平、终吉、利

rule.yi: 周易尚占八卦断例里，这十五个卦的断辞说病平安、顺利：乾「问病获安」，既济「病者安康」，革「孕病皆吉」，贲「病安婚遂」，渐「病疾渐安」，豫「病者获安」，解「病者安宁」，随「疾病安康」，家人「病讼无忧」，益「词病俱平」，颐「讼吉病安」，鼎「婚成病利」，比「讼病解散」，萃「病讼终吉」，咸「利讼利病」。
rule.en: In the judgments by example of the Zhouyi Shangzhan the line of each of these fifteen hexagrams says that illness fares peacefully and well: Qian (Heaven), 'asking about illness: safety is gained'; Jiji, 'the sick are at peace and in health'; Ge, 'pregnancy and illness are both auspicious'; Bi (Adornment), 'the sick are safe, marriage is achieved'; Jian (Gradual Progress), 'illness gradually settles'; Yu, 'the sick gain peace'; Xie, 'the sick are at ease'; Sui, 'illness is eased and health returns'; Jiaren, 'neither illness nor lawsuit brings worry'; Yi (Increase), 'lawsuit and illness are both calm'; Yi (Nourishment), 'the lawsuit is auspicious and the illness safe'; Ding, 'marriage is made, illness fares well'; Bi (Union), 'lawsuit and illness are dissolved'; Cui, 'illness and lawsuit end auspiciously'; Xian, 'favourable to lawsuits and favourable to illness'.

en: The household is at peace and in health.
Asking about illness: safety is gained.
Asking about office: a change of post.
What is planned will surely succeed.
All that is sought is obtained.
Jiji (Already Across) means having crossed over.
Travel by boat meets no delay.
The sick are at peace and in health.
Those in a lawsuit find it resolved.
Going out and coming in are free of worry.
The house suits repair and building.
Going out and coming in are bright and smooth.
Pregnancy and illness are both auspicious.
Misfortune is wiped out and blessing is born.
Public and private affairs are both favourable.
Fields and silkworms ripen to harvest.
The lawsuit disperses and the pregnancy comes to birth.
The sick are safe and marriage is achieved.
Jian (Gradual Progress) means advancing step by step.
Nobles are pleased and office is glorious.
The person is safe and wealth gathers.
The traveller is on the road.
Pregnancy: a noble son is born.
Illness is eased and health returns.
In all divining of the person and fate,
blessing and long life are without limit.
is the image of founding a household.
Neither illness nor lawsuit brings worry.
Calling on nobles and seeking office,
Suits divining the person and dwelling.
Lawsuit and illness are both calm.
Good for oneself and beneficial to others.
Heaven and Earth unite in virtue.
Nourishment should follow what is right.
The lawsuit is auspicious and the illness safe.
Wealth flourishes and salary is abundant.
Public affairs are clear and calm.
The household is quiet and at rest.
It is a vessel for cooking.
Seeking office: complete in all ten parts.
The person is fortunate and the dwelling flourishes.
Marriage is made and illness fares well.
Seeking a matter: entrust it to someone,
Officials and nobles are thriving and strong.
The person and dwelling are safe and sound.
In all one plans and works,
Things depend only on sincerity in oneself.
The person and wealth are both auspicious.
Where there is influence there is response.
The dwelling and the person have joy.
Favourable to lawsuits and favourable to illness.
Though the way of Xian goes through,
it needs all the more uprightness.

dispute.yi: 贲卦这里说「病安婚遂」，别的书却把贲列进占病的凶卦：卜筮元龟一段（LY.ILL.DYTJ.15）和阐奥歌章第五首（LY.ILL.CA.06）都有贲，天玄赋（LY.ILL.TXF.06）说贲「切忌世身入墓」（有条件的），增删卜易（LY.ILL.ZS.01）转述的「断之必死」的十个卦里也有贲。书里没有裁决。
dispute.en: Of these, the line of Bi (Adornment) says 'the sick are safe, marriage is achieved', yet other books put Bi among the ominous hexagrams for illness: the passage of the Bushi Yuangui (LY.ILL.DYTJ.15) and the fifth poem of the Chan'ao Gezhang (LY.ILL.CA.06) both have Bi, the Tianxuan Fu (LY.ILL.TXF.06) says of Bi 'above all avoid the Self or the Body entering the tomb' (conditional), and the ten hexagrams of 'judge death' reported in the Zengshan Buyi (LY.ILL.ZS.01) include Bi. The books do not decide.

note.yi: 这十五行的说法有轻有重：乾、既济、豫、解、随说得最干脆（获安、安康、安宁），渐是「渐安」（慢慢好），萃是「终吉」（最后吉），革、家人、益、颐、比、咸、鼎的病只是和别的事并说（「孕病皆吉」「病讼无忧」），没有单独给病一个断语；「词病俱平」的「词」是词讼、官司。「利讼利病」「婚成病利」的「利」是有利。各行里别的词组（田蚕、官司、婚姻、孕、出行等）对问病没有用处，但一并录在这里，是为了让每一行保持完整、可以对着原书查。书里同一个卦有两个同音的名字（乾和谦，益和颐，贲和比，蹇和渐），英文名后面括号里写的是卦的意思，用来区分。原文「媾」「畜」等写法见各行。上面比较各卦用词轻重的话是编者的归纳，不是书里的话。
note.en: The statements of these fifteen lines range from light to heavy: Qian (Heaven), Jiji, Yu, Xie and Sui are the most outright (gain safety, at peace and in health, at ease); Jian (Gradual Progress) says 'gradually settles' (getting better slowly), and Cui says 'ends auspiciously' (auspicious in the end); for Ge, Jiaren, Yi (Increase), Yi (Nourishment), Bi (Union), Xian and Ding illness is only named together with other matters ('pregnancy and illness are both auspicious', 'neither illness nor lawsuit brings worry') without a verdict of its own; the 'ci' of 'ci and illness are both calm' is a lawsuit or pleading. The 'favourable' of 'favourable to lawsuits and favourable to illness' and 'marriage is made, illness fares well' is 'to the advantage of'. The other phrases of each line (fields and silkworms, lawsuits, marriage, pregnancy, travel and so on) are not useful to a question on illness but are all kept here so that each line stays whole and can be checked against the original book. Some hexagram names in the book have a homonym (Qian for Heaven and for Humility, Yi for Increase and for Nourishment, Bi for Adornment and for Union, Jian for Obstruction and for Gradual Progress), and the parenthesis after the English name gives the meaning of the hexagram to tell them apart. The variant ways of writing a name in the original, such as the 'union' character for Gou, are seen in the lines themselves. The comparison of the strength of the words used in each hexagram above is the editor's summary and not the book's own words.

units.chapter_en: Chapter of Judgments by Example for the Eight Palaces
units.title: 八卦断例·占病逢姤、遁、晋、丰、师、井、夬：病者难安、迁延、难瘥、沉滞、迟瘥、稽迟、迟延

rule.yi: 周易尚占八卦断例里，这七个卦的断辞说病难好、拖得久：姤「病者难安」，遁「病者迁延」，晋「病者难瘥」，丰「病人沉滞」，师「病人迟瘥」，井「问病稽迟」，夬「病讼迟延」。
rule.en: In the judgments by example of the Zhouyi Shangzhan the line of each of these seven hexagrams says that illness is hard to mend and drags on: Gou, 'the sick will find it hard to be at peace'; Dun, 'the sick one drags on'; Jin, 'the sick will find it hard to recover'; Feng, 'the sick one is weighed down and lingering'; Shi, 'the sick recover late'; Jing, 'asking about illness: delay and slowness'; Guai, 'illness and lawsuit are delayed'.

en: Any plan is sure to meet with an encounter.
Seeking office: the office is glorious.
Seeking wealth: the wealth comes as wished.
The sick will find it hard to be at peace.
Marriage: do not take the bride.
As for divining about a traveller,
he is indeed on the road.
A lawsuit can end in reconciliation.
Asking about a betrothal: it will not come about.
Fields and silkworms yield very little.

yi: 财运平平，只是稍微平顺一点。
en: Advancing oneself will surely be achieved.
The traveller has not yet arrived.
The sick will find it hard to recover.
Wealth is level, only slightly so.
Favourable to office and favourable to nobles.
The sick one is weighed down and lingering.
In all divining of the household,
it is half bright and half dim.
but seeing a noble draws his anger.
Do not ask about the traveller.
The household has calamity and hardship.

yi: 把本事藏起来，等待时机。
en: Asking about illness: delay and slowness.
Asking about marriage: obstruction and delay.
Keep the tools hidden and wait for the time.
Marriage and pregnancy are auspicious and prosperous.

dispute.yi: 丰、夬两卦的轻重，几本书说得不一样。别的书把丰、夬列为占病的凶卦，甚至是「十死」：阐奥歌章第三首（LY.ILL.CA.03）、第五首（LY.ILL.CA.06）、卜筮元龟一段（LY.ILL.DYTJ.15）、天玄赋（LY.ILL.TXF.06）、增删卜易转述的十卦（LY.ILL.ZS.01）里都有丰和夬；周易尚占这里丰只是「病人沉滞」，夬只是「病讼迟延」，是病拖得久，没有说死。同样，丰在这里是「利官利贵、婚姻有成」的卦。程度不同，书里没有裁决。
dispute.en: The books do not agree on how heavy Feng and Guai are. Other books list Feng and Guai among the ominous hexagrams for illness, even among the 'ten deaths': the third (LY.ILL.CA.03) and fifth (LY.ILL.CA.06) poems of the Chan'ao Gezhang, the passage of the Bushi Yuangui (LY.ILL.DYTJ.15), the Tianxuan Fu (LY.ILL.TXF.06) and the ten hexagrams reported in the Zengshan Buyi (LY.ILL.ZS.01) all have Feng and Guai; here in the Zhouyi Shangzhan Feng is only 'the sick one is weighed down and lingering' and Guai only 'illness and lawsuit are delayed', that is, illness that drags on, with no word of death. Likewise Feng is here a hexagram of 'favourable to office and to nobles, marriage is achieved'. The degree differs, and the books do not decide.

note.yi: 这七行的病句都是「拖」：难安、迁延、难瘥、沉滞、迟瘥、稽迟、迟延，没有一个说死；姤的「病者难安」最重（难得平安），夬是病和官司一起拖。「沉滞」是沉重、拖着不好，「稽迟」是拖延迟缓，「迁延」是一拖再拖。姤卦在原书里写作「媾」（「媾者遇也」），这里照原文；「卜筮行人 端的在路」是说占行人，他确实还在路上，和病无关。「求官谒贵」（井）这个词组只有事项、没有断语，原文如此。「财平稍平」（晋）意思不清，译文照字面。
note.en: The illness phrases of these seven lines all speak of dragging on: hard to be at peace, protracted, hard to recover, weighed down, late to recover, delay and slowness, delayed; none speaks of death. The heaviest is 'the sick will find it hard to be at peace' of Gou (hard to gain peace), and for Guai illness and the lawsuit drag on together. 'Weighed down and lingering' is heavy and not getting better, 'delay and slowness' is dragging and slow, and 'drags on' is delay upon delay. In the original book Gou is written with the 'union' character ('that character means meeting'), and the line is quoted as it stands; 'as for divining about a traveller, he is indeed on the road' is about a traveller and not about illness. The phrase 'seeking office, calling on nobles' (Jing) has an affair but no verdict, as in the original. 'Wealth is level, only slightly so' (Jin) is unclear in sense and is translated literally.

units.chapter_en: Chapter of Judgments by Example for the Eight Palaces
units.title: 八卦断例·占病逢坎、噬嗑、蛊、离、困、睽、小过、明夷：病凶、病重、件件遭伤、有惊、有忧

rule.yi: 周易尚占八卦断例里，这八个卦的断辞说病凶险、沉重或有忧：坎「孕病皆凶」，噬嗑「病重讼凶」，蛊「孕吉病凶」，离「病重财轻」，困「宅身孕病件件遭伤」，睽「问病有惊」，小过「官阻病忧」，明夷「占家父病」。
rule.en: In the judgments by example of the Zhouyi Shangzhan the line of each of these eight hexagrams says that illness is ominous, heavy or a worry: Kan, 'pregnancy and illness are both ominous'; Shihe, 'illness is heavy and the lawsuit is ill'; Gu, 'pregnancy is auspicious, illness is ominous'; Li, 'illness is heavy and wealth is light'; Kun (Confinement), 'dwelling, person, pregnancy, illness: each one is hurt'; Kui, 'asking about illness: there is a fright'; Xiaoguo, 'office is blocked and illness is a worry'; Mingyi, 'divining the household: the father is ill'.

en: Pregnancy and illness are both ominous.
Seeking wealth in business meets robbers.
A boat on the way meets wind.
coming out of danger, one succeeds.
Plans and hopes are safe when kept low.
Illness is heavy and the lawsuit is ill.
Pregnancy is anxious and marriage is lonely.
Remove obstacles and eliminate the wicked:
only those who have the Way.
Disorder will surely be followed by order.
Pregnancy is auspicious; illness is ominous.
Marriage is made and wealth profits.
Divining the dwelling does not suit.
Marriage and lawsuit: nine parts in ten succeed.
Illness is heavy and wealth is light.
A word to the one who divines:
keep to one's lot and the ordinary.
The three bodies are at odds with one another.
Asking about illness: there is a fright.
Marriage: the two are not matched.
Xiaoguo (Small Excess) means a small excess.
What is passed over is not far.
The person and dwelling have a small calamity.
Office is blocked and illness is a worry.
Pregnancy has a fright; marriage is to be avoided.
Divining pregnancy: the mother is in anxiety.
Divining the household: the father is ill.

dispute.yi: 别的书的占病凶卦名单里，同人、需、剥、节、蒙在内，周易尚占对这几个卦的断辞里却没有讲病：同人是「婚孕皆成、所求皆至」，需是「不宜轻举、所谋不成」，剥是「退则获安、进则不利」，节是「身命不宁」，蒙是「却宜占病」（LY.ILL.ZSZ.06）。阐奥歌章第三首（LY.ILL.CA.03）、第五首（LY.ILL.CA.06）、卜筮元龟一段（LY.ILL.DYTJ.15）和增删卜易转述的十卦（LY.ILL.ZS.01）都有同人；需、剥、节见于卜筮元龟一段和阐奥歌章；蒙只见于卜筮全书疾病论（LY.ILL.BSQS.35）。没有说的不等于说了好，这几个卦占病吉凶，周易尚占这一行没有表态。反过来，这里的坎、噬嗑、蛊、离、困、睽、小过，别的凶卦名单里大多没有（只有蛊、困在），是周易尚占独有的断语。书里没有裁决。
dispute.en: Among the other books' lists of ominous hexagrams for illness are Tongren, Xu, Bo, Jie and Meng, yet the lines of the Zhouyi Shangzhan for these hexagrams do not speak of illness: Tongren is 'marriage and pregnancy both succeed, all that is sought arrives', Xu is 'rash moves do not suit, what is planned does not succeed', Bo is 'to withdraw is to gain safety, to advance is unfavourable', Jie is 'the person and fate are unsettled', and Meng is 'but it suits divining illness' (LY.ILL.ZSZ.06). Tongren is in the third (LY.ILL.CA.03) and fifth (LY.ILL.CA.06) poems of the Chan'ao Gezhang, in the passage of the Bushi Yuangui (LY.ILL.DYTJ.15) and in the ten hexagrams reported in the Zengshan Buyi (LY.ILL.ZS.01); Xu, Bo and Jie are in the Bushi Yuangui passage and the Chan'ao Gezhang; Meng is only in the Bushi Quanshu's essay on illness (LY.ILL.BSQS.35). Not saying is not saying good: for the verdict on illness of these hexagrams the line of the Zhouyi Shangzhan takes no position. Conversely, of the hexagrams here, Kan, Shihe, Li, Kui and Xiaoguo are for the most part absent from the other lists of ominous hexagrams (only Gu and Kun (Confinement) are in them), so these verdicts are peculiar to the Zhouyi Shangzhan. The books do not decide.

note.yi: 这八行里，坎「孕病皆凶」、蛊「孕吉病凶」把病和怀孕并说，困是「宅身孕病」四件并说，都是一句话管几件事。明夷「占孕母忧，占家父病」两句对着读：占怀孕时母亲有忧，占家宅时父亲有病；「占家父病」只有四个字，这个读法是按上一句的格式推的。噬嗑一行的「求财且且」「惟道有者」两处意思不清，「道有者」读来像「有道者」的倒文，译文都照字面，没有改字。噬嗑的头两个词组「噬者啮也」「嗑者合也」都是在解释卦名。「婚寡」译作婚姻孤寡，「孕双」译作怀孕得双胎，都是字面的读法。
note.en: In these eight lines, Kan, 'pregnancy and illness are both ominous', and Gu, 'pregnancy is auspicious, illness is ominous', speak of illness and pregnancy together, and Kun (Confinement) names 'dwelling, person, pregnancy, illness' together, each a single phrase covering several matters. For Mingyi the two phrases 'divining pregnancy: the mother is in anxiety' and 'divining the household: the father is ill' are read in parallel: in divining pregnancy the mother is anxious, in divining the household the father is ill; 'divining the household: the father is ill' is only four characters in the book, and this reading is inferred from the pattern of the previous phrase. In the line of Shihe, 'seeking wealth: barely so' and 'only those who have the Way' are unclear in sense, and the second looks like an inverted form of 'those who have the Way'; both are translated literally and no character has been changed. The first two phrases of Shihe, 'Shi means to bite' and 'He means to close together', both explain the name of the hexagram. 'Marriage is lonely' translates the literal 'marriage widowed' and 'twins' of Li translates the literal 'pregnancy double'.

units.chapter_en: Chapter of Judgments by Example for the Eight Palaces
units.title: 八卦断例·占病宜不宜：履「弗占疾病」、大壮「休占讼病」、蒙「却宜占病」；恒「病须疾治」

rule.yi: 周易尚占八卦断例里有四个卦对占病给的是劝告：履卦说不要占疾病，大壮卦说不要占官司和病，蒙卦说不要营谋、倒适合占病，恒卦说病要赶快治。
rule.en: In the judgments by example of the Zhouyi Shangzhan four hexagrams give advice about divining illness rather than a verdict: Lü (Treading) says do not divine illness, Dazhuang says do not divine lawsuits or illness, Meng says one cannot yet scheme but it suits divining illness, and Heng says illness must be treated quickly.

en: The soft treads on the hard.
In a perilous place there is no harm.
Do not ask about official business.
In all one plans and works,
be careful at the start and the venture will prosper.
Four yang lines are strong and full.
Using force gives rise to calamity.
Do not divine lawsuits or illness.
To move is not to hit the mark.
To hold still is to be upright.
Through dimness one nourishes what is right.
Lost things must be sought elsewhere.
Marriage: there is no fated share.
It carries the sense of long constancy.
The person and dwelling both flourish.
A lawsuit is best settled early.
Keeping to the old way is peaceful and harmonious.

dispute.yi: 蒙卦这里说「却宜占病」，卜筮全书疾病论（LY.ILL.BSQS.35）却把蒙列进春天的十死卦。「宜占病」说的是适合拿这一卦来问病，没有说病会好，所以两处不一定正面冲突，合起来看蒙卦占病到底吉凶，书里没有定论。
dispute.en: Of Meng the line here says 'but it suits divining illness', whereas the Bushi Quanshu's essay on illness (LY.ILL.BSQS.35) puts Meng among the ten fatal hexagrams of spring. 'Suits divining illness' says that this hexagram is a fit one with which to ask about illness, and does not say the illness will mend, so the two places need not clash head on; taken together, the books do not settle whether Meng is auspicious or ominous for illness.

note.yi: 「弗占疾病」「休占讼病」是劝人不要占这件事，书里没有说是因为病凶，还是因为这一卦本身不适合问这类事；履卦同一行里还有「危中有救，险处无妨」。「却宜占病」的「却」是转折：上一个词组说「未可营谋」，这一个说倒适合占病。恒卦「病须疾治」里的「疾」是迅速、赶快，不是疾病。
note.en: 'Do not divine illness' and 'do not divine lawsuits or illness' advise against divining this matter, and the book does not say whether this is because illness is ominous or because the hexagram itself is not a fit one for such questions; the same line of Lü (Treading) also has 'in danger there is rescue, in a perilous place there is no harm'. The 'but' of 'but it suits divining illness' is a turn: the previous phrase says 'one cannot yet scheme', and this says that it nevertheless suits divining illness. The 'quickly' of 'illness must be treated quickly' in Heng is the word for swift, not the word for illness.

units.chapter_en: Chapter of Judgments by Example for the Eight Palaces
units.title: 八卦断例·占病逢巽、旅、临：金神为祟、病者祷禳、病犯祟侵

rule.yi: 周易尚占八卦断例里有三个卦的断辞把病和鬼神联在一起：巽卦「惟占病人，金神为崇」，占病人的时候是金神（白虎）在作祟；旅卦「病者祷禳」，病人要祷告、禳解；临卦「病犯崇侵」，病是撞上了鬼神作祟的侵扰。
rule.en: In the judgments by example of the Zhouyi Shangzhan three hexagrams link illness with spirits: Xun, 'only in divining a sick person: a Metal spirit (the White Tiger) is the curse'; Lü (the Traveller), 'the sick should pray and perform exorcism'; Lin, 'illness meets the encroachment of a curse'.

en: Act in accord with the time.
Favourable to wealth and to marriage.
Favourable to office and to nobles.
The person is at ease and a lawsuit is settled.
Fields give harvest and silkworms thrive.
Only in divining a sick person:
a Metal spirit is the curse.

yi: 在外的人不要指望（归来）。
en: It is the image of being on a journey.
Keeping to the usual is unfavourable.
The lawsuit disperses and marriage is made.
Pregnancy comes to birth and prisoners are freed.
The sick should pray and perform exorcism.
Do not look for the traveller.

yi: 病，遇到鬼神作祟的侵扰。
en: Wealth and office are both auspicious.
Plans and hopes are in step with one's peers.
Illness meets the encroachment of a curse.

note.yi: 巽、临两处原文写的是「崇」（崇高的崇），按上下文是作祟的「祟」，译文按「祟」（鬼神降灾）译，书里没有标注。「金神」按这一部前面「十一、定六神」的「白虎金神」（第 461 行）是白虎，这里「金神为崇」是白虎作祟；别的书里金神常和七煞连称（LY.ILL.EL.34、EL.47），那是另一个意思，这里没有用。「祷禳」是祈祷、禳解（用仪式把灾禳除）。「病犯崇侵」读作病是触犯了、遇到了鬼神作祟的侵扰。三行里别的词组照录。
note.en: In Xun and Lin the original writes the character for 'lofty' where the context calls for the character for 'curse'; the translation reads it as 'curse' (harm sent by a spirit), and the book gives no mark. By 'Section 11: Fixing the Six Spirits' earlier in the same part ('the White Tiger is the Metal spirit', line 461) the 'Metal spirit' is the White Tiger, so 'a Metal spirit is the curse' here is the White Tiger afflicting; in other books the Golden Spirit is often named together with the Seven Killings (LY.ILL.EL.34, EL.47), which is another sense and is not used here. 'Pray and perform exorcism' is to pray and to dispel the calamity by rites. 'Illness meets the encroachment of a curse' reads the illness as having offended or run into the invasion of a curse sent by a spirit. The other phrases of the three lines are kept as they stand.
